correctness.rationale: Map each n-bit word to concatenation of the increasing lists of values tagged 1 then 0. Every nonidentity at-most-one-descent permutation has a unique word; only n+1 prefix-tag words collapse to identity, making total variation error O(n/2^n) and cardinality 2^n-n. The unique descent is FO definable using position adjacency and value decrease, yielding interpretation of tag word in value order; conversely position order is FO from the tag predicate. FO binary word languages have aperiodic deterministic automata; under uniform fair bits each recurrent class of the random-letter transition matrix must be aperiodic (else every letter transition cyclically advances its period classes and contradicts eventual stabilization of word transitions), giving rational finite Markov limits. For any a/b choose b equal-length inner binary words and cross-bifix-free patterns 0^K 1 s_i 1^K, K=d+1; the first occurrence of any pattern is equiprobable among b types via terminal replacement, misses vanish exponentially, and earliest-hit event is FO, giving a/b. Independent checks of 11950 small binary-word and pattern cases passed; proof covers arbitrary denominators and n→∞.
